results.question: What does error KST-2044 mean and how do I fix it?
results.expected_answer: The data source refused the connection because the Kestrel IP addresses are not on its allowlist. Add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11; adding only one causes intermittent errors.

answer.answer: Error KST-2044 means that the data source refused the connection from Kestrel, usually because the database only accepts connections from an allowlist of IP addresses and the Kestrel addresses are missing from it. To fix this, ask the customer to add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist of their database or firewall.

citations.label: C3
citations.quote: Your data source refused the connection from Kestrel.

citations.label: C3
citations.quote: the database only accepts connections from an allowlist of IP addresses, and the Kestrel addresses are missing from it.

citations.label: C3
citations.quote: ask the customer to add both 203.0.113.10 and 203.0.113.11 to the allowlist of their database or firewall.

results.question: A user gets KST-4012 when accepting an invitation. What should support tell them?
results.expected_answer: There is no free seat. An Admin must free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or upgrade. The same invitation then works if it is less than 7 days old.

answer.answer: Support should explain that an Admin of the workspace must remove a member to free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or move to a larger plan. Once a seat is free, the same invitation link will work again as long as it is less than 7 days old.

citations.label: C2
citations.quote: explain that an Admin of the workspace must remove a member to free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or move to a larger plan. Once a seat is free, the same invitation link works again as long as it is less than 7 days old.

results.question: What happens, step by step, when a customer's card payment fails?
results.expected_answer: E-mail to the Owner and billing contact, retries after 1, 3 and 7 days, then a 21-day grace period (everything works), then read-only, then suspension at 60 days. Nothing is deleted.

answer.answer: The documents contain conflicting information regarding the exact automated retry schedule, grace periods, and subsequent steps when a payment fails (for instance, C3 mentions retrying after 1 day, 3 days, and 7 days with a 14-day grace period, while C5 mentions a 21-day grace period and subsequent suspension after 60 days, and C4 mentions a 14-day grace period). Therefore, a single step-by-step process cannot be reliably determined from the provided text.

results.question: Which plans include single sign-on, and how does an admin set it up?
results.expected_answer: Business and Enterprise. An Admin opens Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel SP metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, pastes the IdP metadata URL back, tests with one Admin, then enforces it.

answer.answer: Single sign-on (SAML) is included on the Business and Enterprise plans. To set it up, an Admin goes to Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel.

citations.label: C1
citations.quote: On the Business and Enterprise plans, workspaces can use single sign-on with any SAML 2.0 identity provider. To set it up, an Admin opens Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel.

results.question: I lost my phone and I can't log in anymore. What can I do?
results.expected_answer: Use a backup code. Without one, ask a workspace Admin to reset your second factor. If you are the only Admin or the Owner, contact support from the account's e-mail address; identity verification can take up to 2 business days.

answer.answer: If you no longer have your authenticator device, you can use one of your backup codes at the second-factor prompt and then set up two-factor authentication again from Profile → Security. If you do not have your authenticator device or any backup code, you should ask an Admin of your workspace to reset your second factor from Settings → Members, so you can set it up again at your next sign-in. If you are the only Admin or the workspace Owner, you must write to support from the e-mail address registered on your account.

citations.quote: If you no longer have your authenticator device, use one of your backup codes at the second-factor prompt, then set up two-factor authentication again from **Profile → Security**.

results.question: Can I get a refund on my annual plan 45 days after it renewed?
results.expected_answer: Yes, under the current (March 2026) policy: annual plans are refundable within 60 days of renewal, pro-rated from the request date. The old 2025 policy allowed only 30 days.

answer.answer: Yes, annual plans can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. Since 45 days is within this 60-day window, you can request a refund, which will be pro-rated for the unused full months of the annual period.

citations.label: C2
citations.quote: Annual plans can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. The refund is pro-rated from the date of the request: you are refunded the unused full months of the annual period.
